guarantees.claim: state_sel_o, add_rk_sel_o, key_full_sel_o, key_dec_sel_o, key_words_sel_o, and round_key_sel_o are each driven as the bitwise OR of all corresponding mr_*[i] array entries for i in [0, Sp2VWidth-1], after initial zero assignment.
mr_err is driven to 1 when for any index i, state_sel_o does not equal mr_state_sel[i] or any other *sel_o does not equal its respective mr_*[i]; otherwise mr_err remains 0 (default).

assumptions.claim: All mr_* signal array elements are driven to identical values during normal, fault-free operation.
assumptions.cond: when mr_err is used for fault detection
assumptions.risk: False mr_err assertion may cause unnecessary error handling or masking of a real fault.

assumptions.claim: mr_* signal inputs contain only valid logic levels (0/1) and have widths exactly matching the corresponding *SelWidth parameters.
assumptions.risk: X or Z propagation could cause spurious mr_err assertion or undefined simulation behavior.

uncertain_points.claim: If Sp2VWidth equals 0, the for-loops become empty, all *sel_o remain 0, and mr_err stays 0 regardless of actual mr_* values, disabling fault detection.
uncertain_points.risk: An undetected fault could compromise control integrity or security within the AES cipher.

uncertain_points.claim: mr_err is a combinational output; a transient mismatch on mr_* may produce a glitch that a clocked receiver could miss if not properly synchronized.
uncertain_points.cond: when mr_* signals exhibit transient discrepancies
uncertain_points.risk: A brief fault could go unnoticed, reducing detection coverage.

uncertain_points.claim: No explicit mitigation or assertion guards against the Sp2VWidth=0 case, leaving unclear whether a design with zero redundancy is intentionally supported.
uncertain_points.risk: Unintended use of Sp2VWidth=0 could silently remove fault detection.
